stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when running on Apple Silicon via Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and lower memory consumption.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for enhanced performance.
This update specifically targets and optimizes execution on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, signaling ongoing optimization efforts.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is bringing powerful AI capabilities directly to the user's personal devices.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New attack vector identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attackers can distribute malicious payloads across multiple Pull Requests (PRs) to evade detection.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safety and deployment of capable but untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing and retaining sensitive PII from training data.
Focuses on 'unlearning' techniques, specifically challenging the current paradigm which only evaluates removal at the output level.
Introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of localization for LLM unlearning.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to address complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, thereby improving locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces RECONTEXT (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their actual capacity to leverage that information.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data, such as PII.
It critiques existing 'localize-first, unlearn-second' methods by pointing out that current benchmarks only test output-level erasure.
The paper introduces 'LACUNA' as a new testbed to evaluate the true precision of knowledge removal (unlearning) within LLMs.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to address complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, improving locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs generating unsafe outputs even after alignment training.
Proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system that uses an external model's verifier signal.
Demonstrates that this threshold-based monitoring approach is competitive in safety evaluations (e.g., red teaming).

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a novel data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high inference cost of DiTs, which is exacerbated by multi-step sampling and large parameter counts.
Overcomes a major limitation of prior quantization methods by handling activation shifts across different timesteps and prompts without requiring re-calibration.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's effectiveness is demonstrated as competitive in mathematical reasoning and red teaming evaluations.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS infostealer, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware represents a growing trend in targeted Mac-specific cyber threats.
The discovery highlights the increasing sophistication of malware targeting Apple ecosystems.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to permit supersonic airliners to fly over US cities.
The key condition for this approval is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This development signals a potential shift in commercial aviation, allowing for faster, longer-range travel within the US.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, and shows competitive performance.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across 900+ characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in complex video narratives.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from privileged teacher models causes overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
Aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by modulating disagreement during the self-distillation process.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like backtracking and SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The work focuses on SE-RRMs, which are symbol-equivariant and show improved extrapolation capabilities for larger problem sizes.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents versus off-the-record (OTR) responses under identical conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method addressing limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from a teacher model can cause overfitting and hinder cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning by mitigating the negative effects of privileged information in self-distillation.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for controllable simulated agents designed for realistic traffic simulation.
The agents learn a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from discounted returns, enabling interpretable control.
This controllability allows engineers to isolate variables and test autonomous systems safely without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking costly human annotations.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Uses the LLM's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels for self-supervision.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks behave under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, a key area for scaling ML with decentralized data.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It proposes 'LACUNA,' a testbed designed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not the internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based programming tasks that are poorly suited for traditional code.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs for these tasks, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to detect emergent, unprompted objectives.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of relational context on LLM communication.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in complex video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during reasoning.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly attend to visual inputs during self-correction.
Aims to improve the ability of models to translate feedback into grounded corrections, especially for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates if scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) alone can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study compares LLM compute scale against general capability benchmarks to understand simulation gaps.
It questions whether simulation fidelity is intrinsically linked to general LLM capabilities or requires separate research focus.

stories.title: My credential rule reported 842 secrets in vercel/ai. The real count was 0.
stories.author: ofri-peretz
bullet_points: A security scanning tool (credential rule) generated a high number of false positives (842 findings) when scanning a Vercel project.
The false positives were primarily non-sensitive code artifacts like TypeScript union-type literals and error class names, not actual hardcoded credentials.
The article discusses the technical challenge of moving from context-blind regex scanning to context-aware detection, particularly in the context of AI-generated code.

stories.title: What Google's "Microservices Are Dead" Paper Actually Said (And What It Missed About AI)
stories.author: zxpmail
bullet_points: The article analyzes a 2023 HotOS paper by Google researchers regarding the state of microservices.
It specifically critiques the paper for potentially overlooking the impact and integration of modern AI technologies.
The discussion is relevant to advanced software architecture and large-scale systems design at major tech companies.
